stories.headline: United States forces hit Iranian military targets after attacks on shipping and American troops
stories.body:
United States forces began striking military targets inside Iran at noon on Tuesday. US Central Command announced that the strikes targeted the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. It said the operation responded to attempted attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. US Central Command said forces also reacted to attacks against American service members. About 20% of the world's oil passes through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm Island on the northern side of the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian news agency Nour News reported explosions in the port city of Bandar Abbas. Nour News also reported explosions in the port city of Chabahar. Iranian state media said US strikes hit a fishmeal factory on Qeshm Island. Strikes also hit a fishing pier in Sirik. State media said a maritime tower in Sirik was hit too. US strikes also hit an area outside Jiroft Airport.

The Iranian Red Crescent reported that four people died in Sirik. It said a four-year-old child was among those killed. Missile shrapnel hit a wedding celebration in Sirik. The Red Crescent said that more than 50 people were injured. US Navy Captain Tim Hawkins said the US military never targets civilians. Hawkins said that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps does target civilians.

The Revolutionary Guard launched a barrage of ballistic missiles at a US Marine base in Aqaba, Jordan. Iranian forces launched the missiles in response to the attack in Sirik. The Jordanian Armed Forces reported no deaths from the missile strike near Aqaba. Jordan said no injuries resulted from the attack.

US President Donald Trump posted a warning on social media. Trump said Iran would be hit again at a much harder level if it retaliates. He said the next strikes would also be at a higher level.

A Memorandum of Understanding in June had declared an end to fighting. That earlier fighting had killed thousands of people in Iran and Lebanon. Fighting began after US and Israeli strikes started on February 28. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian spoke in Bishkek about the agreement. Pezeshkian said Iran would immediately reciprocate if the US returns to its commitments. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf also issued a warning. Qalibaf said no one will export oil if enemies try to stop Iran's Persian Gulf oil exports.

The strikes caused a reaction in global financial markets. Japan's 10-year bond yield reached 3%. That yield reached 3% for the first time since 1996 after the market reaction. US national government debt has risen above $40 trillion. The US Embassy in Qatar urged Americans in the Middle East to exercise heightened vigilance. The embassy warned about potential flight cancellations and travel disruptions.

claims.text: US Central Command announced that US forces began striking Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in Iran at 12:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday.
US Central Command stated that strikes on IRGC targets were launched in response to attempted attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against US service members.
Approximately 20% of the world's oil passes through the strategic waterway of the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm Island on the northern side of the Strait of Hormuz during the US attacks.
Iranian news agency Nour News reported explosions in the port cities of Bandar Abbas and Chabahar.
Iranian state media reported US strikes hit a fishmeal factory on Qeshm Island, a fishing pier and maritime tower in Sirik, and an area outside Jiroft Airport.
The Iranian Red Crescent reported four people, including a four-year-old child, were killed and more than 50 injured when missile shrapnel hit a wedding celebration in Sirik, Iran.
US Navy Captain Tim Hawkins stated that the US military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC.
The IRGC launched a barrage of ballistic missiles at a US Marine base in Aqaba, Jordan, in response to the attack in Sirik.
The Jordanian Armed Forces reported no deaths or injuries resulted from the Iranian missile strike near Aqaba.
US President Donald Trump stated on social media that Iran would be hit again at a much harder and higher level if it retaliates against the US strikes.
A June Memorandum of Understanding declared an end to fighting that killed thousands in Iran and Lebanon since US and Israeli strikes began on February 28.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated in Bishkek that Iran would immediately reciprocate if the US returns to its commitments under the June memorandum of understanding.
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf warned that if the enemy attempts to prevent Iran from exporting oil from the Persian Gulf, no one will be able to export oil.
Japan's 10-year bond yield reached 3% for the first time since 1996 following the market reaction to US strikes in Iran.
US national government debt has risen above $40 trillion.
The US Embassy in Qatar urged Americans in the Middle East to exercise heightened vigilance regarding potential flight cancellations and travel disruptions.

stories.headline: Germany blames Russia for Leipzig airport drone attack and orders consulate closed
stories.body:
German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt announced that Russia was responsible for an August 4 drone attack. He said Russia carried out the attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

Security forces discovered an explosive drone near Ukrainian cargo planes at the airport on August 4. The drone was attached to a Ukrainian cargo plane. It carried 600 grams of explosives. The device failed to detonate because of a faulty detonator.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul announced the ordered closure of the Russian consulate in Bonn. Germany also announced it will terminate the contract for the Russian House cultural centre in Berlin. Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said Moscow would respond in a mirror-image fashion.

German investigators reported finding double-digit numbers of explosive devices near a power substation in Brandenburg. They said the devices were an attempt to cause a regional power outage. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha warned that the attack is part of Russia's deliberate strategy toward Europe. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte declared full solidarity with Germany after the attack. Germany is backing a European Commission sanctions package covering 1,600 companies linked to Russia.

claims.text: German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt announced that Russia was responsible for an August 4 drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport.
An explosive drone discovered near Ukrainian cargo planes at Leipzig/Halle Airport on August 4 failed to detonate due to a faulty detonator.
The drone discovered attached to a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig airport on August 4 was carrying 600 grams of explosives.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul announced the ordered closure of the Russian consulate in Bonn.
Germany announced it will terminate the contract for the Russian House cultural centre in Berlin.
Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova stated Moscow would respond in a mirror-image fashion to Germany's diplomatic measures.
German investigators reported finding double-digit numbers of explosive devices near a power substation in Brandenburg in an attempt to cause a regional power outage.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha warned that Russia's hybrid attack at Leipzig airport is part of a deliberate strategy toward Germany and Europe.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte declared full solidarity with Germany following the Russian hybrid attack in Leipzig.
Germany is backing the European Commission's 22nd sanctions package covering 1,600 companies and organizations linked to Russia.

a facility in an electrical grid that changes voltage

stories.headline: Russian strikes kill at least 12 people in Kyiv while targeting Ukrainian railways
stories.body:
Russian strikes killed at least 12 people in Kyiv overnight. The attacks injured more than a dozen people. Six Ukrainian railway workers were killed when a missile hit a locomotive depot in Kyiv on Tuesday. A Russian ballistic missile hit the depot.

Four people were killed in Boryspil near Kyiv when a strike hit a residential building. A 26-year-old Indian national was killed in Boryspil on his birthday. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged Russian President Vladimir Putin to move toward peace. Modi spoke to Putin in Kyrgyzstan.

Russia has struck Ukraine's railway network more than 1,500 times in 2026. Those strikes damaged 249 carriages and 492 locomotives. Since Russia's full-scale invasion began, 58 Ukrainian railway staff have been killed. At least 318 railway workers have been injured. Ukrzaliznytsia operates 15,000 miles of track as Ukraine's largest company.

Ukrainian air defences shot down 187 out of 218 drones launched by Russia. Air defences also downed five Iskander ballistic missiles, two Banderol cruise missiles, and five Kalibr cruise missiles. A Ukrainian drone strike hit the Russian Baltic Sea port of Ust-Luga, triggering a fire. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Ukrainian drones will continue operating over Russian airspace. According to AFP analysis, Russian forces captured 35 square miles of Ukrainian territory during August 2026. US defence manufacturer Lockheed Martin produces about 600 Pac-3 Patriot interceptor missiles per year.

claims.text: Overnight Russian strikes on Kyiv killed at least 12 people and injured over a dozen.
Six Ukrainian railway workers were killed when a Russian ballistic missile hit a locomotive depot in Kyiv on Tuesday.
Four people were killed in Boryspil, near Kyiv, when a Russian strike hit a residential building.
A 26-year-old Indian national was killed in Boryspil on his birthday during Russian strikes.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged Russian President Vladimir Putin in Kyrgyzstan to move from endless war toward peace.
So far in 2026, Russia has struck Ukraine's railway network more than 1,500 times, damaging 249 carriages and 492 locomotives.
Since Russia's full-scale invasion began, 58 Ukrainian railway staff have been killed and at least 318 injured.
Ukrzaliznytsia operates 15,000 miles of track and employs 170,000 workers, making it Ukraine's largest company.
Ukrainian air defences shot down 5 Iskander ballistic missiles, 2 Banderol cruise missiles, 5 Kalibr cruise missiles, and 187 out of 218 drones launched by Russia.
A Ukrainian drone strike hit the Russian Baltic Sea port of Ust-Luga, triggering a fire.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Ukrainian drones will continue operating over Russian airspace.
According to AFP analysis, Russian forces captured 35 square miles of Ukrainian territory during August 2026.
US defence manufacturer Lockheed Martin produces approximately 600 Pac-3 Patriot interceptor missiles per year.

stories.headline: Nepal flash flood death toll reaches 1,050 as rescuers search for missing workers
stories.body:
Flash floods in Nepal killed 1,050 people by Tuesday evening. Around 4,000 people remain missing. Nearly 600 foreigners from 39 countries are among the missing.

The flash flood began in Tibet on August 26. A catastrophic collapse of rock and ice sent debris through two river systems into Nepal. Debris flowed through the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems. Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority reported 987 bodies recovered by Tuesday morning. The agency said 11,814 people were rescued. It reported 3,916 people missing at that time. Rescuers prioritized searching for at least 900 missing workers at 12 hydropower projects. More than 600 hydropower workers were feared trapped in tunnels north of Bidur.

An Indian tunnel rescue team established a foothold in tunnels in Chilime using improvised floats. India's Ministry of External Affairs reported that 163 Indian nationals were rescued from Nepal. It said 151 Indian nationals left China as of September 1. India sent a consignment of 37.5 tonnes of relief material, medicines, and food packets. That delivery brought total Indian emergency aid to 47.5 tonnes.

Five Australians were confirmed safe, reducing the number of unaccounted-for Australian citizens to 38. Australia's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade received nearly 800 calls. Australia dispatched 18 personnel to Nepal. Africa Disaster Relief searched for six missing South Africans along the border between Nepal and China.

claims.text: By Tuesday evening, September 1, the death toll in Nepal reached 1,050 with around 4,000 people missing, including nearly 600 foreigners from 39 countries.
The flash flood began in Tibet on August 26, 2026, when a catastrophic collapse of rock and glacial ice sent water and debris through the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems into Nepal.
Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority reported 987 bodies recovered, 3,916 people missing, and 11,814 rescued as of Tuesday morning, September 1.
Rescuers in Nepal prioritized the search for at least 900 workers missing from 12 hydropower projects.
More than 600 hydropower workers were feared trapped underground in tunnels north of Bidur after the disaster.
An Indian tunnel rescue team established a foothold in hydropower tunnels in Chilime using improvised floats and innovative methods.
India's Ministry of External Affairs reported that 163 Indian nationals had been rescued from Nepal and 151 Indian nationals had left China as of September 1.
India dispatched a consignment of 37.5 tonnes of relief material, medicines, and food packets to Nepal, bringing total Indian emergency aid to 47.5 tonnes.
Five Australians were confirmed safe following the Nepal floods, reducing the number of unaccounted-for Australian citizens from 43 to 38.
Australia's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade received nearly 800 calls regarding the Nepal floods and dispatched 18 personnel to Nepal.
Africa Disaster Relief launched a search for six South Africans who went missing in the floods along the border between Nepal and China.

a quantity of goods delivered to a recipient

stories.headline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urges Shanghai Cooperation Organisation members to dismantle terror networks
stories.body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed leaders at the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit on September 1. Modi spoke in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, urging member states to dismantle terrorist ecosystems.

Summit leaders adopted the Bishkek Declaration. The declaration called for an inclusive government in Taliban-ruled Afghanistan. Leaders also expressed concern over the conflict in West Asia. Modi said the crisis in West Asia must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy. He said the conflict should not be resolved on the battlefield. SCO leaders adopted joint initiatives on combating drug addiction and conserving biodiversity. Leaders also agreed to create the SCO Green Technology Corridor for 2026-2030. Pakistan assumed the role of SCO chair for the 2026-2027 term.

Modi held a brief exchange with Chinese President Xi Jinping during the summit in Bishkek. He also held a bilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trade between India and Russia rose from around $13 billion in 2021 to nearly $60 billion in 2025. Indian imports of Russian crude oil largely drove that trade growth.

In a video message from Kyrgyzstan, Modi repeated his appeal for Indian citizens to change spending habits. Modi urged citizens to avoid foreign vacations. He asked people to avoid destination weddings abroad. Modi also urged citizens to avoid non-essential gold purchases. The unit value of gold imports to India moderated to $2.8 per kg. That price was 47% higher than a year earlier. The unit value was down from $3.5 per kg in June.

Modi praised India's economic resilience during his summit remarks. India's gross domestic product grew at 7.8% in the April-June quarter. That GDP growth surpassed the Reserve Bank of India's forecast of 7%.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated at the SCO summit that the crisis in West Asia must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy rather than on the battlefield.

Pakistan assumed the role of Shanghai Cooperation Organisation chair for the 2026-2027 term.

Trade between India and Russia rose from around $13 billion in 2021 to nearly $60 billion in 2025, largely driven by Indian imports of Russian crude oil.
In a video message from Kyrgyzstan, Prime Minister Narendra Modi repeated his appeal for citizens to avoid foreign vacations, destination weddings abroad, and non-essential gold purchases.
The unit value of gold imports to India moderated to $2.8 per kg, 47% higher than a year earlier, down from $3.5 per kg in June.
India's GDP grew at 7.8% in the April-June quarter, which Prime Minister Narendra Modi cited while praising economic resilience.
